# 12-Week Post-MI Conditioning Programme

**Client Profile:** 58-year-old male, 6 months post-myocardial infarction, cleared for Phase II cardiac rehab.

**Key Constraints:**
- HR cap: ~115 bpm (70% of age-predicted max, 220-58=162)
- No Valsalva manoeuvre — teach continuous exhalation on exertion
- No maximal lifting — RPE cap of 5-6/10 throughout, never above 7
- Full gym access

**Session Framework (all weeks):**
- 10-min warm-up: brisk walk + dynamic mobility + breathing drills
- Conditioning block (aerobic)
- Resistance block
- 10-min cool-down: walk-down + static stretch + parasympathetic breathing (4-7-8)
- HR and RPE logged every block; BP pre/post ideally

---

## PHASE 1 — Foundation & Reconditioning (Weeks 1–4)

Goal: re-establish movement patterns, build aerobic base at low intensity, ingrain diaphragmatic breathing, monitor tolerance.

### Week 1 — Baseline
**3 sessions, non-consecutive days.**

Each session:
- **Aerobic:** 15 min treadmill walking, HR 90–100 bpm, RPE 3–4
- **Resistance (full body, machines only):**
  - Seated leg press — 2 × 12 (very light, RPE 4)
  - Chest press machine — 2 × 12
  - Seated row machine — 2 × 12
  - Machine shoulder press — 2 × 10
  - Supported bodyweight sit-to-stand — 2 × 10
- **Core/breathing:** Dead bug 2 × 8/side; supine diaphragmatic breathing 3 min

### Week 2
- **Aerobic:** 20 min treadmill or upright bike, HR 95–105 bpm
- **Resistance:** same lifts, 2 × 12, small load bump if RPE ≤ 4 last week
- Add: Cable pallof press 2 × 10/side

### Week 3
- **Aerobic:** 22–25 min, HR 100–110 bpm, RPE 4–5. Introduce 1-min light incline intervals (2–3 reps).
- **Resistance:** 3 × 10 on all main lifts
- Add: Glute bridge 2 × 12; farmer carry (light DBs, 20 m × 2)

### Week 4 — Deload/Assess
- Reduce volume ~30%; reassess HR recovery (should drop ≥12 bpm in 1 min post-effort), BP response, any symptoms.
- Confirm readiness to progress.

---

## PHASE 2 — Aerobic Development & Strength Build (Weeks 5–8)

Goal: extend aerobic duration, introduce interval work under HR cap, transition select machines to free weights/DBs, build work capacity.

### Week 5
- **Aerobic:** 25 min steady-state, HR 105–115 bpm. Alternate treadmill / recumbent bike / elliptical across sessions (3×/wk).
- **Resistance (upper/lower split acceptable, or continue full-body 3×):**
  - Goblet squat (light KB) — 3 × 10
  - DB bench press — 3 × 10
  - Chest-supported DB row — 3 × 10
  - DB Romanian deadlift (hip hinge focus, submaximal) — 2 × 10
  - Half-kneeling landmine press — 2 × 8/side
  - Suitcase carry — 2 × 20 m/side
- Emphasise **exhale on the concentric** every rep.

### Week 6
- **Aerobic:** Introduce structured intervals — 4 × 3 min at HR 110–115, 2 min active recovery at 90–95. Total ~25 min including warm/cool.
- **Resistance:** 3 × 10, modest load progression (RPE stays ≤ 6)
- Add: Split squat (supported) 2 × 8/side

### Week 7
- **Aerobic:** 30 min continuous, HR 105–115; OR intervals 5 × 3 min.
- **Resistance:** 3 × 8–10, progress load where RPE < 5
- Add: Cable chop 2 × 10/side; TRX/inverted row 2 × 8

### Week 8 — Deload/Reassess
- Volume down ~30%, intensity maintained
- Retest: 6-min walk distance, HR recovery, RPE at fixed workloads. Communicate progress to cardiology team if applicable.

---

## PHASE 3 — Consolidation & Functional Capacity (Weeks 9–12)

Goal: maintain the HR ceiling but improve efficiency (more work at same HR), introduce light unilateral and loaded carries, build habits sustainable long-term.

### Week 9
- **Aerobic (3×/wk):** 30–35 min mixed modality; one session tempo (steady at 110–115), one intervals (5 × 3 min), one cross-training (bike or rower, no max pulls).
- **Resistance (2 full-body sessions/wk):**
  - Goblet or box squat — 3 × 8
  - DB incline press — 3 × 8
  - One-arm DB row — 3 × 8/side
  - DB RDL — 3 × 8
  - Half-kneeling cable row — 2 × 10/side
  - Farmer carry — 3 × 30 m
  - Dead bug + pallof combo — 2 × 8

### Week 10
- **Aerobic:** Extend one steady session to 35–40 min at HR 105–110 (comfortable conversation pace).
- **Resistance:** 3 × 8, modest load bump. Introduce **step-ups** (low box) 2 × 8/side.

### Week 11 — Peak Load Week
- **Aerobic:** 3 sessions — one 40-min steady, one intervals 6 × 3 min, one 30-min cross-training
- **Resistance:** 3 × 8 across the board; still RPE ≤ 6. Add light **sled push** (walking pace, no straining) 3 × 20 m if available.

### Week 12 — Reassess & Transition
- Volume back ~40%; intensity maintained
- Full reassessment:
  - Resting HR & BP trends
  - HR recovery post 3-min moderate effort
  - 6-min walk test
  - Subjective wellbeing (Borg RPE, sleep, mood)
- Plan Phase III (community-based maintenance) with prescribed HR zones expanded pending cardiologist review.

---

## Nutrition Guidance (share with client; refer to dietitian for individualised plan)

- **Pattern:** Mediterranean-style — vegetables, legumes, oily fish 2–3×/wk, olive oil, whole grains, nuts.
- **Protein:** 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight/day, spread over 3–4 meals to support lean mass during reconditioning.
- **Sodium:** < 2,300 mg/day; watch processed foods.
- **Saturated fat:** < 7% total kcal; replace with mono/polyunsaturated.
- **Alcohol:** ≤ 1 drink/day or abstain.
- **Fluids:** 2–2.5 L/day; pre-session hydration important — dehydration raises HR at fixed workload.
- Time carbohydrates around training sessions to support performance without excess intake.

---

## Recovery Protocol

- **Sleep:** target 7–9 h; consistent bed/wake times. Poor sleep → elevate next-day resting HR (rescheduling trigger).
- **Daily monitoring:** morning resting HR (log); a spike of >7 bpm above baseline = deload that day's session.
- **Breathwork:** 5 min box-breathing or 4-7-8 nightly; parasympathetic tone is a priority.
- **Active recovery days:** 20–30 min flat walking on off-days.
- **Mobility:** 10-min routine 2×/wk — thoracic spine, hips, ankles.
- **Symptoms warranting session termination and physician contact:** chest pain/pressure, unusual dyspnoea, dizziness, palpitations, pallor, cold sweat, HR > 115 at low workload, BP drop with exercise.

---

## Coaching Notes for You

1. **Never chase load.** RPE and HR govern progression, not weight on the bar.
2. **Teach breathing first, every session.** Continuous exhale on effort — no held breaths under any load.
3. **Warm up longer than feels necessary.** Ischaemic hearts do not tolerate abrupt demand shifts.
4. **Cool down is non-negotiable** — abrupt cessation can trigger arrhythmia; 10 minutes minimum walking down.
5. **Keep a session log** with HR at rest, mid-session, peak, and 1-min recovery. Trend these — improvement in recovery HR is your best marker.
6. **Liaise with the cardiology/rehab team** before Phase 3 to confirm HR ceiling can be raised, and before adding any higher-intensity or heavier loading beyond week 12.

**Client:** 58-year-old male, 6 months post-MI. Assume ~85 kg (adjust to actual). Sedentary-to-lightly-active baseline moving into structured training.

**Aligned to:** AHA dietary guidelines, DASH, Mediterranean pattern — the strongest evidence base for secondary prevention post-MI.

⚠️ **Refer to a registered dietitian for individualised prescription, especially if the client is on statins, anticoagulants (warfarin — vitamin K considerations), antihypertensives, or has comorbid diabetes/CKD.**

---

## 1. Energy & Macronutrient Targets

**Total daily energy:** ~2,000–2,300 kcal during Phase 1, ~2,200–2,500 kcal Phases 2–3 (adjust for weight goal; most post-MI clients benefit from modest fat loss if BMI > 25).

## 2. Foundational Food Framework

### Eat Daily
- **Vegetables:** 5+ servings, half the plate at lunch/dinner. Emphasise leafy greens (nitrates → BP), cruciferous, tomatoes, peppers.
- **Fruit:** 2–3 servings, prioritise berries, apples, citrus, pears (soluble fibre + polyphenols).
- **Whole grains:** oats, barley, quinoa, brown rice, wholegrain bread — 3–5 servings. **Oats and barley (β-glucan) are especially LDL-lowering.**
- **Legumes:** beans, lentils, chickpeas — 4+ servings/week minimum, ideally daily.
- **Nuts/seeds:** small handful (~30 g) daily — walnuts, almonds, flaxseed, chia. Walnuts specifically have RCT evidence post-MI.
- **Extra virgin olive oil:** 2–4 tbsp/day as primary added fat (PREDIMED evidence).
- **Fluids:** 2–2.5 L/day, mostly water. Green tea acceptable and beneficial.

### Eat Weekly
- **Oily fish:** 2–3 servings/week (salmon, mackerel, sardines, trout, herring) — ~500 mg EPA+DHA/day equivalent.
- **Poultry:** 2–3 servings, skinless.
- **Eggs:** up to 6/week (recent evidence supports moderate intake even post-MI).
- **Dairy:** low-fat, unsweetened — yoghurt (probiotic), kefir, small amounts of cheese for flavour.

### Limit
- **Red meat:** ≤1 serving/week, lean cut.
- **Processed meats:** essentially eliminate (bacon, sausages, deli meats — high sodium + nitrates + saturated fat).
- **Refined grains and sugar:** white bread, pastries, sweetened drinks — occasional only.
- **Ultra-processed foods:** ready meals, crisps, biscuits — high in sodium, trans fats, additives.
- **Alcohol:** ≤1 standard drink/day, or abstain. **Post-MI: leaning toward abstinence is safer**, especially if on antiarrhythmics or anticoagulants.
- **Coffee:** 1–3 cups/day is fine; monitor if HR/BP sensitive.

## 6. Sodium Reduction — Practical Strategies

Most sodium excess is hidden, not from the salt shaker:
- **Buy fresh, cook at home.** Ready meals average 800–1,500 mg sodium per portion.
- Read labels: <120 mg/100 g = low; >600 mg/100 g = high.
- Rinse tinned beans/lentils (removes ~40% sodium).
- Replace salt at the table with lemon, vinegar, garlic, herbs, spices, chilli.
- Watch these hidden sources: bread, breakfast cereals, soups, cheese, sauces, condiments, cured meats, olives, pickles.

**Week 1–2:** Focus on **addition, not restriction** — add veg to every meal, add oily fish 2×/wk, swap refined grains for whole. Don't overhaul at once.

**Week 3–4:** Introduce sodium awareness; label-reading exercise together.

**Week 5–8:** Tighten saturated fat, refine portion sizes, structure training-day nutrition.

# Supplementary Light Strength Block — Deconditioning Response

**Rationale:** Client reports subjective deconditioning — likely reflecting muscle loss from six months of reduced activity post-MI (sarcopenia risk is real at 58 with a sedentary interval). We can safely add **low-load, high-quality strength work** without breaching cardiac constraints, because:

- Light loads (RPE 4–5) with controlled tempo do **not** elevate HR significantly if breathing is managed.
- Resistance work has strong secondary prevention evidence in post-MI populations.
- The current programme is aerobic-dominant; adding a dedicated strength emphasis addresses his complaint directly.

**Non-negotiables remain:**
- HR cap 115 bpm
- No Valsalva — exhale on every concentric, no held breath
- RPE ceiling 5–6, never above 7
- No max singles, no failure sets, no eccentric-overload work
- No isometric holds >10 seconds (BP spike risk)
- No overhead pressing with heavy load (BP response) — light DB overhead is fine
- No inversions or head-below-heart positions under load

## Key Coaching Points to Reinforce

1. **Breathing is the intervention.** Exhale on effort, every rep. Any breath-holding = stop the set, reset.
2. **Tempo controls intensity as much as load.** A slow, controlled 3-1-2 rep at moderate weight is safer and more productive than fast reps with lighter load.
3. **RPE 5 means "I could do 5 more reps."** If he could only do 2 more, it's too heavy — drop the load next set.
4. **No grinding reps.** The moment tempo breaks down or breathing halts, the set ends.
5. **Log HR post-set for the first 2 weeks** to build a picture of his response to loaded work. This is data you want.
6. **Deconditioning recovers fast.** He should feel meaningfully stronger by Week 8. Reassure him — the sensation of weakness is not a red flag, it's the starting line.

# Revised Programme — Weeks 8–12 (Phase III Progression)

**New parameters from cardiologist:**
- HR cap raised to **~138 bpm** (85% of 162 age-predicted max)
- **Brief, controlled Valsalva permitted at moderate loads** — this unlocks proper bracing on compound lifts
- Still **no max-effort lifting** — RPE ceiling now 7–8 (no true 1RM, no failure sets)
- Still no maximal isometrics, no breath-holding beyond 2–3 seconds

**What this actually changes:**
1. Aerobic zone widens — we can prescribe genuine moderate-vigorous work, not just low-moderate.
2. Compound lifts can be loaded meaningfully — hinge and squat patterns become the anchor.
3. Interval work can be prescribed by target HR, not just RPE.
4. Strength adaptations will accelerate — expect real progress, not just reconditioning.

**What doesn't change:**
- Continuous exhale on effort remains the **default** — Valsalva is a **tool for the hardest working sets only**, not a habit.
- Warm-ups and cool-downs stay long (10 min each). Ischaemic hearts still don't like abrupt transitions.
- Symptom vigilance is unchanged. Higher HR ceiling ≠ higher risk tolerance.
- Log HR, RPE, and recovery HR every session.

## Valsalva Coaching — Do This Properly

This is the biggest technical change in the programme. Get it right.

**Permitted:**
- Brief brace with partial breath-hold (1–3 sec) during the sticking point of a heavy compound lift — squat, deadlift, row
- Only on working sets at RPE 6+
- Only after the client can demonstrate exhale-on-effort reliably

**Not permitted:**
- Breath-hold on light warm-up sets
- Breath-hold on overhead pressing
- Breath-hold longer than 3 seconds
- Breath-hold combined with straining or grinding a rep
- Any brace on machines or isolation work

**Cue sequence for a properly braced squat:**
1. Big breath in through nose at top
2. Brace 360° into belt/torso
3. Descend
4. **Exhale forcefully through pursed lips as you drive up through the sticking point** (this is a partial Valsalva, not a full hold)
5. Full exhale at top, reset breath

You want a **"grunt-out" style** rather than a held breath. This is the safest way to permit intra-abdominal pressure for cardiac patients cleared for moderate Valsalva.

# Interval Conditioning Block — Phase III

**Rationale:** With HR ceiling now 138 bpm, we have genuine room to prescribe structured intervals across multiple energy systems. Interval training in post-MI Phase III populations has strong evidence for improving VO₂peak, endothelial function, and HR recovery — often more efficiently than steady-state alone. The key is **structured prescription** (target HR zones, defined work:rest, deliberate progression) rather than "harder for a bit, then easier."

**Guiding principles:**
- All intervals prescribed by **target HR**, not RPE alone — heart rate is the safety governor
- Warm-up is longer than the interval block for the first 3 weeks — never skip
- Cool-down is non-negotiable — abrupt cessation post-interval is the highest-risk moment
- **Two interval sessions per week maximum** — one aerobic-dominant, one anaerobic-tolerant
- Modality rotation reduces orthopaedic load and keeps cardiovascular stimulus varied
- If HR recovery in the rest period doesn't drop by ≥15 bpm in 2 min, the next work bout is delayed or cut

---

## HR Zones (based on 162 bpm max)

| Zone | % Max HR | BPM | Purpose | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z1 Recovery | <65% | <105 | Warm-up, cool-down, active recovery | 2–3 |
| Z2 Aerobic base | 65–75% | 105–121 | Steady-state, fat oxidation | 3–4 |
| Z3 Tempo | 75–82% | 121–133 | Aerobic threshold, sustainable hard | 5–6 |
| **Z4 Threshold** | **82–88%** | **133–142** | **Interval work — anaerobic threshold** | **7** |
| Z5 VO₂ | >88% | >142 | **Off-limits** — exceeds cardiologist cap | — |

**Working ceiling: 138 bpm.** Z4 window is effectively 133–138 for this client.

---

## Modality Options — Ranked by Cardiac Suitability

1. **Upright/recumbent bike** — smoothest HR response, easy to modulate, low orthopaedic cost. **Preferred for early intervals.**
2. **Treadmill (incline walking → jogging)** — natural, weight-bearing benefit, HR responds predictably to gradient
3. **Elliptical** — low impact, whole-body, good for variety
4. **Rower** — excellent stimulus but **technique-sensitive**; poor rowing = Valsalva + BP spike. Only if he demonstrates clean form.
5. **Ski erg** — similar to rower; use sparingly
6. **Sled push (walking pace)** — good option Weeks 11–12, HR responds cleanly, no impact

**Avoid for now:** stair mill at high speed (HR overshoots fast), assault bike at high output (BP spike), any modality with breath-holding tendency.

---

## Interval Session Types

### Type 1: Long Aerobic Intervals (LAI)
**Purpose:** Build sustainable aerobic capacity at threshold.
- Work: 3–5 min in Z3–low Z4 (125–135 bpm)
- Rest: 2–3 min active in Z1 (walking)
- Total work: 15–20 min
- Frequency: Once/week — the "Monday" slot

### Type 2: Short Threshold Intervals (STI)
**Purpose:** Higher HR exposure at the ceiling, in tolerable doses.
- Work: 60–90 sec in Z4 (133–138 bpm)
- Rest: 2 min active in Z1
- Total work: 8–12 min
- Frequency: Once/week — later in the block

### Type 3: Cardiac Rehab Style Ramps (CRR)
**Purpose:** Sub-threshold conditioning with structured HR climb.
- Progressive 2-min stages climbing Z2 → Z3 → low Z4, then step-down
- 20–25 min total
- Useful for reintroduction weeks and deload

**We are not doing HIIT in the classical sense** — no all-out 30-sec efforts, no Tabata protocols, no work above 138. Those exceed the cardiologist's cap.

---

## 5-Week Progression (Weeks 8–12)

Replaces the aerobic prescriptions in the previous plan.

### WEEK 8 — Reintroduction
Test week — one interval session only.

**Monday — CRR (introduction)**
- 10 min warm-up bike Z1→Z2
- 2 min at 110 bpm
- 2 min at 118 bpm
- 2 min at 125 bpm
- 2 min at 130 bpm
- 2 min at 118 bpm
- 2 min at 130 bpm
- 2 min at 125 bpm
- 2 min at 118 bpm
- 2 min at 110 bpm
- 10 min cool-down
Total ~40 min. Watch HR climb rate and recovery between stages.

**Friday — steady Z2**, 35 min at 115–120 bpm.

---

### WEEK 9 — First Structured Intervals

**Monday — LAI (bike)**
- 12 min warm-up (Z1 → Z2, gradual ramp)
- **4 × 3 min at 125–132 bpm**, 2 min recovery at 105 bpm between
- 10 min cool-down + breathing
- Total ~40 min

**Friday — Steady + Finisher (treadmill incline walk)**
- 25 min at Z2 (115–122 bpm), 3–5% incline
- 3 × 90 sec at 128–133 bpm, 90 sec recovery
- 10 min cool-down
- Total ~45 min

**Coaching focus this week:** establish HR recovery baseline. Between-interval HR should drop 15+ bpm in 2 min. If it doesn't, extend rest.

---

### WEEK 10 — Extend Duration

**Monday — LAI (bike or elliptical)**
- 10 min warm-up
- **5 × 3 min at 128–135 bpm**, 2 min recovery at 105 bpm
- 10 min cool-down
- Total ~45 min

**Friday — STI introduction (treadmill or bike)**
- 12 min warm-up (extended for first STI session)
- **6 × 90 sec at 130–138 bpm**, 2 min recovery at 105 bpm
- 12 min cool-down (also extended)
- Total ~45 min

**First exposure to the top of the HR ceiling.** Watch him closely on efforts 4–6 — HR often creeps upward on later bouts. Cut a rep if 138 is exceeded.

---

### WEEK 11 — Peak Interval Week

**Monday — LAI extended (bike or treadmill incline)**
- 10 min warm-up
- **4 × 4 min at 130–138 bpm**, 2 min recovery
- 10 min cool-down
- Total ~45 min
- **Biggest single aerobic stimulus of the block.** Should feel genuinely hard but sustainable.

**Friday — Mixed Interval (bike preferred)**
- 10 min warm-up
- 2 × 3 min at 128–133 bpm, 2 min recovery
- 4 × 60 sec at 133–138 bpm, 90 sec recovery
- 2 × 3 min at 128–133 bpm, 2 min recovery
- 10 min cool-down
- Total ~45 min

Watch him carefully this week — first true peak week at Phase III intensities. If HR recovery lags on Friday session, cut the final long interval.

---

### WEEK 12 — Deload & Reassess

**Monday — CRR reassessment**
- Repeat Week 8 CRR protocol exactly
- Compare HR at each stage vs Week 8 — should be **5–10 bpm lower at matched workload** (this is the adaptation you're looking for)
- Compare HR recovery between stages

**Friday — Easy Z2**
- 30 min steady at 115–122 bpm, conversational
- 10 min cool-down

Debrief data with client: workload achieved at HR 125 (Week 8 vs Week 12), HR recovery time, subjective breathlessness at daily activities.

---

## Session-by-Session Safety Protocol

Every interval session, without exception:

**Pre-session (5 min):**
- Resting HR check — should be within 7 bpm of morning baseline. If elevated, downgrade session.
- BP check if equipment available.
- Symptom screen: sleep quality, chest sensations, energy, medication adherence.

**During work bouts:**
- HR displayed continuously (chest strap preferred over wrist optical — more accurate at higher HR)
- **Hard cap 138 bpm** — do not tolerate overshoots. Reduce workload immediately.
- Talk test — should be able to say 3–4 words per breath at Z4. If mute, too hard.
- Coach cues: exhale rhythm, upright posture, relaxed shoulders and jaw

**During rest bouts:**
- Keep moving — no standing still, no sitting
- Log HR at 1 min and 2 min into recovery
- If HR recovery <10 bpm in 2 min → extend rest or terminate session

**Post-session:**
- Full 10-min active cool-down — walk down HR to <100 bpm before stopping
- 5 min seated, then re-check HR and BP
- Should feel pleasantly tired, not hollowed out

---

## Weekly Load Distribution (Weeks 9–11)

| Day | Session | Approx duration | Cardiovascular emphasis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mon | **Interval** (LAI) | 40–45 min | High — Z3/low Z4 |
| Tue | Rest or 30-min walk | — | Z1 |
| Wed | Strength A | 50 min | Low — Z2 |
| Thu | Rest or mobility | — | — |
| Fri | **Interval** (STI or mixed) | 40–45 min | High — Z4 |
| Sat | Strength B | 50 min | Low — Z2 |
| Sun | Rest | — | — |

Two hard cardiovascular days, two strength days, three recovery days. Never stack intervals on consecutive days.

---

## Integration Notes with Strength Programme

- **Never** run an interval session in the 24 hours **before** a heavy compound lifting day. Move it or lighten the strength session.
- Monday intervals → Wednesday strength gives 48h buffer ✓
- Friday intervals → Saturday strength is tight; keep Saturday's opening lift at RPE 6, not 7
- If he reports poor recovery, drop Friday intervals before dropping Saturday strength — cardiovascular adaptation persists longer than strength stimulus
- **Fuelling matters more now** — 40–60 g carbs 60–90 min pre-interval session, or he'll bonk mid-session and HR response will be misleading

---

## Progression Rules (for programming beyond Week 12)

Only progress interval load when:
1. **HR at matched workload has dropped ≥5 bpm** vs previous exposure
2. **HR recovery ≥15 bpm in 2 min** consistently across all bouts
3. **RPE at target HR has fallen** by 1 point (e.g., 138 bpm now feels RPE 6, was RPE 7)
4. **No symptoms** across the prior 2 weeks
5. Sleep and morning resting HR trending stable or downward

Progression options, in order of aggression:
- Add one work bout (safest)
- Extend work bout duration by 30 sec
- Reduce rest duration by 30 sec
- Add a second interval session **only** with cardiologist review

Do not compound progressions — one variable per week.

---

## Red Flags Specific to Interval Work

Terminate session immediately if:
- HR exceeds 138 despite reducing workload
- HR fails to recover below 115 within 3 min of stopping a work bout
- New arrhythmia sensation (skipped beats, irregular pulse)
- Chest discomfort, jaw or arm referral, unusual dyspnoea
- Light-headedness on transitions between work and rest
- Sudden pallor or cold sweat
- **Post-session HR that stays elevated >20 min** — this is unusual and warrants same-week cardiology contact

Escalate to cardiologist within a week if:
- Two consecutive interval sessions with poor HR recovery
- Rising trend in resting HR over 5+ mornings
- Subjective decline in exercise tolerance despite programme adherence

The higher ceiling gives us more room to work — it does not remove the ceiling above the ceiling. Everything about post-MI conditioning rewards patience and punishes ambition. Progress him steadily, log everything, and he'll be in a completely different place at Week 12 than he was at Week 1.

# Immediate Programme Rollback — Return to Phase II Parameters

**This is a clinical event, not a programming setback.** Chest tightness during exertion in a post-MI patient is a red flag requiring cardiology re-evaluation before any further progression. Your job now is to keep him moving safely, preserve conditioning, and not add any variables that complicate the cardiologist's assessment.

---

## First Actions (Do These Today)

1. **Confirm cardiology appointment is booked.** If not already scheduled, urge him to contact his cardiology team today — not next week. Chest tightness on exertion in a post-MI patient warrants prompt review, not routine follow-up.
2. **Document the incident in detail** — you'll be asked, and the cardiologist will want it:
   - Date, time, session type, modality
   - Workload at onset (speed, gradient, watts, HR at onset)
   - Character of the sensation: tightness vs pressure vs pain; central vs radiating; duration
   - Associated symptoms: breathlessness, sweating, nausea, dizziness, palpitations
   - Time to resolution after stopping
   - Any medication taken (GTN spray if prescribed)
   - HR and BP if you captured them
3. **Ask the client directly** about any symptoms since — even mild ones, at rest or on daily activity. Note anything reported.
4. **Confirm medication adherence** — missed doses of beta-blocker, statin, or antiplatelet are common precipitants and worth flagging to the cardiologist.
5. **Hold all training until you have a documented plan.** Even the "safe" Phase II sessions below should not commence until:
   - He has been reviewed by cardiology, **or**
   - Cardiology has explicitly said "continue Phase II conditioning while awaiting review"

If cardiology says stop entirely pending investigation — you stop entirely. Walking only, no structured sessions.

---

## Revised Parameters — Effective Immediately

| Parameter | Previous (Phase III) | **New (Phase II Restored)** |
|---|---|---|
| HR ceiling | 138 bpm (85%) | **115 bpm (70%)** |
| Valsalva | Brief permitted | **None — continuous exhale only** |
| RPE ceiling | 7–8 | **5, hard cap** |
| Intervals | Yes, structured | **None** |
| Compound lifting (squat/deadlift with bar) | Yes, RPE 7 | **Suspended** |
| Session frequency | 4/week | **2–3/week** |
| Session duration | 45–50 min | **30–40 min** |
| Rest between sets | 75–90 sec | **90–120 sec** |
| Symptom vigilance | Baseline | **Elevated** — check-in every 10 min |

**Add:** HR and BP check at start, mid-session, and end of every session. Log everything. This data helps the cardiologist too.

---

## Interim Training Plan (Until Cardiology Reviews)

Assumes cardiology has said "continue light activity" but not yet formally reassessed. If they say stop, stop.

### Weekly Structure
| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Light aerobic + machine resistance |
| Tue | Rest or 20-min flat walk |
| Wed | Rest |
| Thu | Light aerobic + machine resistance |
| Fri | Rest or 20-min flat walk |
| Sat | Optional light aerobic (walk only) |
| Sun | Rest |

Two structured sessions per week. No strength days as previously written. No intervals. No rowing, no sled, no compound barbell work.

### Session Template (~35 min)

**Warm-up (10 min)**
- 5 min slow walk on treadmill, 0% incline, HR <100
- Cat-camel × 8
- Glute bridge × 10
- Band pull-apart × 10
- Wall slide × 8
- Diaphragmatic breathing × 6 breaths

**Aerobic (15 min)**
- Upright or recumbent bike, HR 95–110 bpm, RPE 3–4
- **Do not exceed 115 bpm under any circumstances**
- Coach checks in verbally every 5 min — any chest sensation, breathlessness, dizziness → stop

**Resistance (machines only, ~15 min)**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RPE | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seated leg press | 2 × 12 | 4 | Light load, controlled tempo, exhale on press |
| Chest press machine | 2 × 12 | 4 | Full exhale each rep |
| Seated row machine | 2 × 12 | 4 | |
| Lat pulldown | 2 × 12 | 4 | |
| Machine leg curl | 2 × 10 | 4 | |
| Supported sit-to-stand | 2 × 10 | 3–4 | |

**Machines only.** No free weights this block. Machines control the movement path, remove the balance/bracing demand that encourages breath-holding, and give predictable HR response.

**No standing overhead pressing. No loaded hinging. No unilateral loaded work.**

**Cool-down (10 min)**
- 5 min slow walk, ramp HR down to <95
- Doorway pec stretch
- Standing hamstring stretch
- Child's pose
- 4-7-8 breathing × 6 rounds
- **Do not let him leave until HR is <100 and BP is at or near baseline**

---

## What to Watch For (Every Session)

**Terminate session immediately for:**
- Any chest sensation — tightness, pressure, discomfort, "heaviness" — even mild
- Referred discomfort: jaw, left arm, upper back, epigastric
- Breathlessness disproportionate to workload
- Dizziness, light-headedness, visual disturbance
- Palpitations or awareness of irregular pulse
- Pallor, cold sweat, nausea
- HR overshoot beyond 115 at low workload (mismatched response — a red flag in itself)
- Failure of HR to recover below 100 within 5 min of stopping

**Any of the above:**
1. Stop, seated recovery
2. Monitor HR and symptoms
3. If symptoms resolve within 5 min at rest → contact cardiology same day for advice
4. If symptoms persist beyond 5 min, or include chest pain not relieved by rest → **call emergency services**. Post-MI patients with unresolving chest pain get an ambulance, not a taxi.
5. Document everything

**Between sessions, ask each time he arrives:**
- Any chest sensations since last session?
- Any at rest? At night?
- Any breathlessness climbing stairs or walking uphill?
- Sleep quality?
- Medication taken as prescribed?
- Any changes to medication from GP or cardiology?

---

## Nutrition — Unchanged, But Emphasise These

The cardiac-focused nutrition plan stays in place — this is exactly the population it was designed for. Reinforce the highest-yield elements during this rollback period:

- **Sodium <2,000 mg/day** — tighten if he's been sloppy. BP control matters more than ever right now.
- **Medication adherence with food** as prescribed (statin timing, beta-blocker with meals if that's his pattern)
- **Alcohol** — recommend abstinence during the review period. It complicates symptom interpretation and can precipitate arrhythmia.
- **Caffeine** — cap at 1–2 cups/day, none within 6 hours of a session. If he's a heavy coffee drinker, this alone can affect HR and symptom reporting.
- **Hydration** — 2 L/day baseline. Dehydration + beta-blocker = orthostatic symptoms that can be mistaken for cardiac events.
- **Suspend creatine** if he was taking it. Not because it's dangerous, but to remove variables during the cardiology assessment.
- **No new supplements** during the review window.

---

## What NOT to Do

- **Do not** try to "test" whether the symptom recurs at a slightly lower intensity. That's a cardiologist's decision, not yours.
- **Do not** progress load or duration until cardiology gives explicit clearance, even if he feels fine.
- **Do not** let him self-progress. Deconditioned clients often push harder to "catch up" after a setback — don't allow it.
- **Do not** reintroduce intervals, Valsalva, or compound lifts on your own authority when he returns to Phase III. Wait for the cardiologist's revised parameters in writing (or documented in his notes).
- **Do not** ignore mild symptoms as "probably nothing." Everything gets reported.
- **Do not** train him if he presents with any active chest symptom, however mild. Send him home, tell him to contact cardiology.

---

## Communicating With Cardiology

Prepare a **one-page summary** for him to bring to the appointment:

- Programme phase and parameters at time of event
- Session detail (modality, workload, HR at symptom onset)
- Symptom description and duration
- Recovery time
- Any prior sessions with lesser symptoms he may not have mentioned
- His current medications (ask him to bring the list)
- What you're currently doing (Phase II parameters, machines only)
- Your questions: revised HR ceiling? Return-to-lifting criteria? Any modalities to avoid? Timeline for reassessment?

The cardiologist will value this. It saves them time, gives them objective data, and demonstrates you're a competent part of his care team.

---

## Return-to-Progression Criteria

**Do not resume Phase III parameters until:**
1. Cardiology has formally reviewed him (imaging, ETT, or clinical review as they see fit)
2. Written or documented clearance to progress
3. New HR ceiling specified in writing
4. Any medication changes stabilised for at least 2 weeks
5. He has completed **4 consecutive Phase II sessions symptom-free** with normal HR and BP response
6. Morning resting HR stable and within normal range for him

Even then, resumption looks like **Week 5–6 of the original programme**, not Week 11. Rebuild the ladder, don't jump back to the top rung.

---

## A Final Note

You did the right thing pulling him back. Chest tightness in a post-MI patient during exertion is exactly the signal this system exists to catch. Recognising it, stopping, and escalating is competent practice — not overreaction.

The most common error at this point is impatience: his, or yours on his behalf. He'll feel fine within a few days and want to push on. Hold the line. The programme can wait. His heart cannot be re-injured cheaply.

Log everything. Communicate with cardiology. Rebuild slowly. That's the whole job right now.

# Safe Activity While at Phase II — Practical Guide

This covers what he can do **inside** your sessions, **outside** your sessions, and what he should **avoid** — until cardiology re-evaluates and gives you new parameters in writing.

**Overarching rule:** if it doesn't push HR above 115, doesn't require breath-holding, doesn't cause any chest sensation, and isn't a novel high-intensity stimulus — it's likely fine. When in doubt, err smaller. This is a maintenance window, not a training window.

---

## Inside Your Sessions — Definitely Safe

Already covered in the rollback plan, but to make it concrete:

**Aerobic modalities (HR cap 115, RPE ≤5):**
- Upright bike ✓ — best first choice, smoothest HR response
- Recumbent bike ✓ — even safer, good for confidence rebuild
- Treadmill flat walking ✓
- Treadmill low-incline walking (up to 3%) ✓
- Elliptical at low resistance ✓

**Resistance work (machines, RPE ≤5, 2 × 12):**
- Seated leg press ✓
- Chest press machine ✓
- Seated row machine ✓
- Lat pulldown ✓
- Machine leg curl ✓
- Machine leg extension ✓ (light)
- Machine shoulder press — **only if seated with back support, light load** ✓
- Cable triceps pushdown, cable biceps curl ✓ (light, isolation, low HR cost)

**Core and mobility:**
- Dead bug ✓
- Bird-dog ✓
- Glute bridge (bodyweight) ✓
- Pallof press with light cable ✓
- Cat-camel ✓
- All standing/seated stretching ✓
- Diaphragmatic and box breathing drills ✓ — actively encourage

**Carries — only if light:**
- Farmer carry with light DBs, short distance, normal breathing ✓ — cap at loads where he can hold a conversation

---

## Outside Your Sessions — Definitely Safe

The goal here is **movement volume without cardiovascular provocation**. NEAT (non-exercise activity thermogenesis) matters more now than structured cardio.

**Walking:**
- Flat walking, any duration, conversational pace ✓
- 20–40 min once or twice daily is ideal
- Keep to flat terrain; avoid hills that push HR above 115
- Cooler parts of the day; avoid extreme heat or cold (both stress the cardiovascular system)

**Daily living:**
- Light gardening (weeding, watering, planting) ✓
- Cooking, food shopping ✓
- Light housework — dusting, tidying, laundry ✓
- Driving (if cardiology hasn't restricted it) ✓
- Sexual activity — generally fine if he can climb two flights of stairs without symptoms, but if in doubt he should confirm with cardiology
- Desk work, reading, hobbies ✓

**Structured low-intensity practice:**
- Yin/restorative yoga ✓ (avoid inversions, avoid held breath poses)
- Tai chi ✓ — genuinely good option, low HR, breathing-centred
- Qigong ✓
- Stretching routines ✓
- Foam rolling ✓ (avoid prone positions that compress the chest for long)

**Mental/recovery work:**
- Meditation, breathing practice ✓ — actively beneficial
- Sleep hygiene work ✓
- Journaling symptoms, energy, mood ✓ — data for cardiology

---

## Grey Zone — Only With Caution

Not banned, but requires monitoring. If any provoke symptoms, stop and report.

**Swimming (leisurely, not lap training):**
- Only if he was a competent swimmer pre-MI
- Cold water can trigger arrhythmia — pool water only, warm
- Cap at 20 min, easy pace
- **Never alone** — always with a companion, ideally at a supervised facility
- If cardiology hasn't specifically cleared swimming, ask them

**Cycling outdoors:**
- Flat, quiet routes only
- Cool weather, not hot
- With a companion
- HR monitor on
- Not yet if he's still symptomatic on the bike indoors

**Golf (with buggy):**
- Fine if walking is flat and he uses the buggy
- Avoid heavy club-swinging as a max-effort motion
- Watch heat exposure

**Light bowls, croquet, gentle recreational activities:**
- Fine, but avoid competitive intensity

**Light DIY:**
- Fine for painting, light carpentry, assembly
- Avoid: overhead work with arms above heart for long periods, heavy lifting, ladder work at height

---

## Avoid Entirely (Until Cardiology Reassesses)

**Cardiovascular:**
- Intervals of any kind — none
- Running, jogging
- Hill walking or hiking on gradient
- Cycling with any hills or headwind battles
- Rowing (technique-dependent, high Valsalva risk)
- Ski erg, assault bike
- Stair climber at pace
- Swimming laps for training
- Any group fitness class (spin, boot camp, HIIT, circuit) — you can't control the intensity
- Cold water immersion, ice baths
- Sauna and steam room — significant cardiovascular stress, especially post-MI

**Resistance:**
- All barbell compound lifts (squat, deadlift, bench, overhead press)
- All heavy DB compound lifts
- Any lift where he might Valsalva — even instinctively
- Overhead pressing with meaningful load
- Loaded hinging (RDL, good morning, kettlebell swing)
- Loaded carries at heavy weight
- Any unilateral loaded work (Bulgarian split squat, loaded lunges)
- Sled push or drag
- Isometric holds beyond 10 seconds
- Bodyweight exercises that involve straining: push-ups to fatigue, pull-ups, dips
- Any resistance work above RPE 5

**Environmental and lifestyle:**
- Heavy meals immediately before activity — pushes HR up, worsens angina threshold
- Activity in extreme heat (>26°C ambient) or cold (<5°C)
- Activity at altitude if travelling
- Activity within 90 min of caffeine, especially strong coffee/pre-workout
- Alcohol before activity — impairs symptom recognition
- Activity when sleep-deprived, unwell, or recovering from any illness
- Emotional stress + exertion combined (arguing on the phone while on the treadmill sort of thing)

**Sexual activity considerations:**
- If chest tightness has recurred at low workload, he should confirm with cardiology before resuming — the "two flights of stairs" rule assumes symptom-free exertion
- Avoid immediately after heavy meals or alcohol
- Report any exertional symptoms in this context to cardiology too

---

## Daily Movement Prescription

A reasonable weekly picture during this holding pattern:

| Day | Structured session | Daily walking | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mon | 35-min gym session | 20 min flat | Stretch 10 min |
| Tue | — | 30 min flat | Tai chi/breathwork |
| Wed | — | 20 min flat | Restorative activity |
| Thu | 35-min gym session | 20 min flat | Stretch 10 min |
| Fri | — | 30 min flat | Breathwork |
| Sat | — | 20–40 min flat | Light social activity |
| Sun | — | 20 min flat | Rest |

**Target:** 150+ min/week of Zone 1–2 activity, spread out, symptom-free. That's the ceiling until cardiology says otherwise.

---

## Signs That He's In A Good Holding Pattern

Over 2–3 weeks of this approach, you should see:
- Morning resting HR stable (±5 bpm of baseline)
- No chest sensations at any intensity or at rest
- No breathlessness beyond what's expected for the workload
- Sleep quality maintained
- Mood and energy stable
- BP (if checked) trending stable
- Enjoyment of daily walking, no exertional anxiety

If those are all in place when cardiology reviews, you're presenting a well-managed patient — which strengthens the case for measured re-progression.

## Signs Something Is Wrong

Escalate to cardiology (not emergency, but same-week) if:
- Any chest sensation returns, at any intensity, even mild
- Symptoms at rest — even fleeting
- New nocturnal symptoms (waking short of breath, chest sensations)
- Resting HR trending upward over 5+ days
- New breathlessness on stairs or daily activities that was previously fine
- Ankle swelling
- Weight gain >2 kg in a few days (fluid retention flag)
- Increased fatigue, reduced tolerance to walks he was managing fine

Escalate to emergency services if:
- Chest pain unrelieved by rest within 5 min
- Chest pain unrelieved by GTN (if prescribed) after two doses 5 min apart
- Chest pain with sweating, nausea, or referred jaw/arm discomfort
- Syncope or near-syncope
- Sudden severe breathlessness at rest
- Palpitations with dizziness

---

## Framing This For The Client

He will likely feel restless. Recently he was doing intervals; now he's on machines and flat walks. Frame this well:

- **This isn't a step backwards, it's a hold.** The programme is paused pending a specialist review — same as any athlete under medical review.
- **The goal this month is data quality**, not fitness gain. Clean sessions, no symptoms, good sleep — that's what the cardiologist needs to see.
- **The floor is high.** He's not detraining to nothing. He's holding roughly Week 4–5 conditioning, which he'll rebuild through quickly once cleared.
- **Symptom honesty is the priority.** Not reporting mild symptoms to preserve the programme is the worst thing he can do. Reinforce that at every session.
- **Patience now is speed later.** A month of holding is nothing against the cost of another cardiac event.

Your job during this window is boring, careful, and unglamorous — and it's the most important coaching you'll do with this client. Hold the line, log the data, wait for cardiology.

# PHASE 2 — AEROBIC DEVELOPMENT & STRENGTH BUILD (Weeks 5–7)

# 12-Week Post-MI Conditioning Programme — Full Consolidated Plan

**Client Profile:** 58-year-old male, 6 months post-myocardial infarction. Started on Phase II cardiac rehab clearance. Progressed to Phase III at Week 8 following cardiology review. Experienced exertional chest tightness during Week 11 intervals — regressed to Phase II parameters pending cardiology re-evaluation.

**This document reflects the programme as actually delivered**, including the mid-programme upgrade to Phase III and the subsequent regression. It is written so any coach picking this up mid-stream can understand what has happened, what parameters apply now, and how to progress once cardiology re-clears.

---

## Parameter History

| Weeks | Phase | HR Ceiling | Valsalva | RPE Cap | Session Freq |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–7 | Phase II | 115 bpm (70%) | None | 5–6 | 3/week |
| 8–10 | Phase III | 138 bpm (85%) | Brief permitted | 7–8 | 4/week |
| 11 (partial) | Phase III | 138 bpm | Brief permitted | 7–8 | 4/week — **event occurred** |
| 11 (post-event) → present | **Phase II restored** | **115 bpm (70%)** | **None** | **5** | **2–3/week** |

**Current status:** Awaiting cardiology re-evaluation. Training continues at Phase II parameters only if cardiology has said "continue light activity while awaiting review." If they have said stop, stop.

---

## Universal Session Framework (All Phases)

- 10-min warm-up: walk + dynamic mobility + breathing drills
- Conditioning and/or resistance block
- 10-min cool-down: walk-down + stretch + parasympathetic breathing
- HR and RPE logged every block
- BP pre/post ideally; mandatory post-event
- Chest-strap HR monitor throughout, not wrist optical

---

# PHASE 1 — FOUNDATION & RECONDITIONING (Weeks 1–4)

**Parameters:** HR cap 115 bpm, RPE ≤5, no Valsalva, machines and light DBs only, 3 sessions/week.

**Goal:** Re-establish movement patterns, build low-intensity aerobic base, ingrain diaphragmatic breathing, monitor tolerance.

## Week 1 — Baseline

3 sessions, non-consecutive days.

**Aerobic:** 15 min treadmill walking, HR 90–100, RPE 3–4.

**Resistance (full body, machines only):**
- Seated leg press — 2 × 12, very light
- Chest press machine — 2 × 12
- Seated row machine — 2 × 12
- Machine shoulder press — 2 × 10
- Supported sit-to-stand — 2 × 10

**Core/breathing:** Dead bug 2 × 8/side; supine diaphragmatic breathing 3 min.

## Week 2

**Aerobic:** 20 min treadmill or upright bike, HR 95–105.
**Resistance:** Same lifts, 2 × 12, small load bump if RPE ≤4 last week.
**Add:** Cable pallof press 2 × 10/side.

## Week 3

**Aerobic:** 22–25 min, HR 100–110, RPE 4–5. Introduce 1-min light incline segments (2–3 reps).
**Resistance:** 3 × 10 on all main lifts.
**Add:** Glute bridge 2 × 12; farmer carry (light DBs, 20 m × 2).

## Week 4 — Deload & Assess

Reduce volume ~30%. Reassess:
- HR recovery (target ≥12 bpm drop in 1 min post-effort)
- BP response
- Any symptoms
- Confirm readiness to progress

---

# PHASE 2 — AEROBIC DEVELOPMENT & STRENGTH BUILD (Weeks 5–7)

**Parameters unchanged:** HR cap 115, RPE ≤6, no Valsalva.

**Goal:** Extend aerobic duration, introduce interval work under HR cap, transition machines to free weights where safe, build work capacity.

**New:** From Week 5, add a fourth session — a dedicated Light Strength Day between aerobic sessions (Wednesday slot).

## Week 5

**Aerobic (2 sessions):** 25 min steady-state, HR 105–115. Rotate treadmill / recumbent bike / elliptical.

**Full-body resistance session (1×/week, paired with aerobic):**
- Goblet squat (light KB) — 3 × 10
- DB bench press — 3 × 10
- Chest-supported DB row — 3 × 10
- DB Romanian deadlift (submax) — 2 × 10
- Half-kneeling landmine press — 2 × 8/side
- Suitcase carry — 2 × 20 m/side

**NEW: Light Strength Day A (Wednesday):**
Warm-up 10 min. Then:
- Goblet squat 3 × 10, RPE 5
- DB bench press 3 × 10, RPE 5
- Chest-supported DB row 3 × 10, RPE 5
- Half-kneeling landmine press 2 × 8/side, RPE 5
- Step-up (low box, bodyweight → light DBs) 2 × 8/side
- Farmer carry 3 × 30 m
- Dead bug 2 × 8/side
Cool-down 10 min.

Tempo 3-1-2, exhale on concentric every rep.

## Week 6

**Aerobic intervals introduced:** 4 × 3 min at HR 110–115, 2 min active recovery at HR 90–95. Total ~25 min including warm/cool.

**Full-body resistance:** 3 × 10, modest load progression (RPE ≤6).
**Add:** Split squat (supported) 2 × 8/side.

**Light Strength Day B (alternating with Day A weekly):**
- DB Romanian deadlift 3 × 10, RPE 5
- Cable seated row 3 × 10, RPE 5
- DB floor press 3 × 10, RPE 5
- Split squat (support, light DBs) 2 × 8/side
- Single-arm DB row 2 × 10/side
- Suitcase carry 3 × 20 m/side
- Pallof press 2 × 10/side

## Week 7

**Aerobic:** 30 min continuous, HR 105–115; OR intervals 5 × 3 min.
**Full-body resistance:** 3 × 8–10, progress load where RPE <5.
**Add:** Cable chop 2 × 10/side; TRX/inverted row 2 × 8.
**Light Strength Day:** 3 × 10, RPE 5, alternate A/B.

---

# PHASE 3 — CARDIOLOGY REVIEW & UPGRADE (Week 8)

**Cardiology re-evaluated at end of Week 7. New parameters granted:**
- HR ceiling raised to 138 bpm (85%)
- Brief, controlled Valsalva permitted at moderate loads
- RPE ceiling raised to 7–8
- Still no max-effort lifting, no failure sets, no true 1RM

## Week 8 — Reassessment & Rebase at New Ceiling

**Treated as transition week, not deload. Baseline data at new ceiling.**

**Testing (spread across the week):**
- Submaximal graded treadmill test to HR 125 — record workload, RPE, HR recovery
- 6-minute walk test — compare to prior baselines
- Load reassessment on compound lifts — working weight for 8 reps at RPE 6
- Grip strength & 30-sec sit-to-stand

**Training this week (3 sessions only):**
- Aerobic steady 30 min, HR 115–125
- Strength A at Week 7 loads, 3 × 8
- Aerobic intervals: 5 × 3 min at HR 125–130, 2 min recovery

---

# PHASE 3 — AEROBIC & STRENGTH PROGRESSION (Weeks 9–11)

**Parameters:** HR cap 138, brief Valsalva permitted, RPE ≤7 (top sets 8 permitted on compound lifts only).

## Weekly Structure

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Aerobic intervals + brief resistance |
| Tue | Rest or 30-min walk |
| Wed | Strength Day A (Squat/Push) |
| Thu | Rest or mobility |
| Fri | Aerobic steady + brief resistance |
| Sat | Strength Day B (Hinge/Pull) |
| Sun | Rest |

## HR Zones (162 bpm max)

| Zone | % Max | BPM | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Z1 Recovery | <65% | <105 | Warm/cool-down, active recovery |
| Z2 Aerobic base | 65–75% | 105–121 | Steady-state |
| Z3 Tempo | 75–82% | 121–133 | Threshold-adjacent |
| Z4 Threshold | 82–85% | 133–138 | Interval ceiling |
| Z5 VO₂ | >85% | >138 | **OFF-LIMITS** |

## Week 9

**Monday — Long Aerobic Intervals (bike):**
- 12 min warm-up
- 4 × 3 min at HR 125–132, 2 min recovery at 105
- 10 min cool-down
- Post-cardio: DB bench 2 × 10, cable row 2 × 10

**Wednesday — Strength A:**
- Back squat (or goblet) 4 × 6, RPE 6–7 (Valsalva permitted top 2 sets)
- DB bench press 4 × 8, RPE 6–7
- Chest-supported DB row 3 × 10, RPE 6
- DB overhead press (seated, back-supported) 3 × 8, RPE 5–6 (exhale on press, no Valsalva overhead)
- Step-up (loaded, 20 cm box) 3 × 8/side, RPE 6
- Farmer carry 3 × 40 m, RPE 6

**Friday — Steady + Finisher (treadmill incline):**
- 25 min at Z2 (115–122), 3–5% incline
- 3 × 90 sec at HR 128–133, 90 sec recovery
- Post: pallof 3 × 10/side, dead bug 3 × 8/side, plank 3 × 30 sec

**Saturday — Strength B:**
- Trap-bar deadlift (or DB RDL) 4 × 6, RPE 6–7 (Valsalva permitted top sets)
- Cable seated row 4 × 8, RPE 6–7
- DB incline bench 3 × 8, RPE 6
- Split squat (with support) 3 × 8/side, RPE 6
- Lat pulldown 3 × 10, RPE 6
- Suitcase carry 3 × 25 m/side, RPE 6
- Pallof press 2 × 10/side

## Week 10 — Load Progression

**Monday — Long Aerobic Intervals:**
- 5 × 3 min at HR 128–135, 2 min recovery

**Wednesday — Strength A:**
- Back squat 4 × 5, RPE 7
- DB bench 4 × 8, load bump
- Step-up 3 × 8/side, heavier DBs
- Rest of session as Week 9

**Friday — Short Threshold Intervals (introduction):**
- 12 min warm-up (extended)
- 6 × 90 sec at HR 130–138, 2 min recovery at 105
- 12 min cool-down (extended)
- First exposure to top of HR ceiling. Cut a rep if 138 exceeded.

**Saturday — Strength B:**
- Trap-bar deadlift 4 × 5, RPE 7
- Cable row 4 × 8, load bump
- Add Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8/side, RPE 6

## Week 11 — Peak Load Week

**⚠️ Event occurred during this week. Programme as originally written below; incident and rollback follow.**

**Monday — Long Aerobic Intervals extended:**
- 4 × 4 min at HR 130–138, 2 min recovery
- Post-cardio: brief resistance supersets

**Wednesday — Strength A:**
- Back squat 5 × 5, RPE 7 (top set)
- DB bench 4 × 6, RPE 7
- One-arm DB row 4 × 8/side, RPE 7
- DB overhead press 3 × 8, RPE 6
- Walking lunge 3 × 10/side, RPE 6
- Farmer carry 3 × 40 m, RPE 7

**Friday — Mixed Interval — CHEST TIGHTNESS OCCURRED:**
- 20 min steady + 5 × 90 sec at HR 130–138 + 15 min steady planned
- **Session terminated. Symptom reported to cardiology. Programme regressed same day.**

---

# EVENT & REGRESSION (Week 11 onward)

## What Happened

Chest tightness during Friday intervals of Week 11. Session terminated. Cardiology notified. Client instructed to book urgent review. Programme regressed to Phase II parameters pending re-evaluation.

## Documentation Provided to Cardiology

- Session detail: modality, workload, HR at symptom onset
- Symptom description: character, duration, associated symptoms, resolution time
- Prior 4 weeks of session data — HR trends, RPE trends, recovery HR
- Current medication list
- Nutrition/lifestyle: sleep, caffeine, alcohol, adherence
- Programme parameters at time of event

**Only proceed with training if cardiology has said "continue light activity while awaiting review." If they say stop, stop entirely — walking only.**

## Session Template (~35 min)

**Warm-up (10 min):**
- 5 min slow treadmill walk, 0% incline, HR <100
- Cat-camel × 8, glute bridge × 10, band pull-apart × 10, wall slide × 8
- Diaphragmatic breathing × 6 breaths

**Aerobic (15 min):**
- Upright or recumbent bike, HR 95–110, RPE 3–4
- **Hard cap 115 bpm**
- Verbal check-in every 5 min for chest sensation, breathlessness, dizziness

**Resistance (machines only, ~15 min):**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Seated leg press | 2 × 12 | 4 |
| Chest press machine | 2 × 12 | 4 |
| Seated row machine | 2 × 12 | 4 |
| Lat pulldown | 2 × 12 | 4 |
| Machine leg curl | 2 × 10 | 4 |
| Supported sit-to-stand | 2 × 10 | 3–4 |

**Machines only. No free weights. No standing overhead pressing. No loaded hinging. No unilateral loaded work.**

**Cool-down (10 min):**
- 5 min slow walk, HR down to <95
- Doorway pec stretch, standing hamstring stretch, child's pose
- 4-7-8 breathing × 6 rounds
- Do not release him until HR <100 and BP near baseline

## Permitted Activity Outside Sessions

**Definitely safe:**
- Flat walking, any duration, conversational pace — 20–40 min once or twice daily
- Light gardening, cooking, shopping, light housework
- Restorative yoga (no inversions, no held-breath poses)
- Tai chi, qigong
- Stretching, foam rolling, breathwork, meditation

**Avoid entirely until re-cleared:**
- All intervals, running, hill work
- Cycling outdoors on hills or against wind
- Rowing, ski erg, assault bike
- Swimming laps, cold immersion, sauna, steam room
- Group fitness classes of any kind
- All barbell compound lifts
